text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"Los Angeles, CA","level":"city","category":"just_cause_eviction","status":"in_force","title":"LA RSO/JCO relocation assistance and Declaration of Intent to Evict for no-fault evictions","requirement":"For no-fault evictions from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or Just Cause Ordinance (JCO), the landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving a termination notice, and must file a copy of the notice with LAHD within 3 days of service. The landlord must also pay relocation assistance per unit (not per tenant), made available within 15 days of service of the written notice. Payment may instead be placed in escrow within the same 15 days. The amount depends on whether the tenant is eligible or qualified, the length of tenancy, and income. Reduced amounts apply to Mom and Pop properties (owner or relative occupancy only) and to single-family dwellings owned by natural persons (JCO only: one month's rent). The landlord may offset accumulated rent against the payment, except where the termination is required by a governmental order to vacate. Not-at-fault reasons listed: owner or relative occupancy, resident manager, demolition or conversion or removal from rental use (Ellis Act for RSO units), governmental order to vacate, HUD recovery before sale, residential hotel conversion, and conversion to affordable housing. Failure to file the Declaration makes the eviction a violation of the RSO or JCO.","key_value":"Chart A (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027): Eligible household $11,000 (under 3 years) or $14,400 (3+ years or low income); Qualified household $23,150 or $27,400; Mom & Pop $10,550 (eligible) or $21,250 (qualified); single-family dwelling owned by a natural person (JCO only) one month's rent. Increases every July 1.","coverage_conditions":"Units covered by the Los Angeles RSO or JCO. Qualified tenant: 62 or older, handicapped or disabled, or with one or more minor dependent children. Mom and Pop reduced amount requires four or fewer units in the building, no use of the provision in the prior three years, an owner with no more than four units plus one single-family home in the City, and an eligible relative who owns no residential property in the City.","exemptions":"Relocation assistance is not required when evicting a resident manager to replace them with another resident manager (a Manager-Tenant may still be entitled), or when evicting due to hazardous conditions caused by a natural disaster not caused by the landlord's negligence.","coverage_logic":{"covers":null,"exempt":null},"subject":"landlord","interaction":null,"yields_to_local":false,"preempts_local":false,"effective_date":null,"effective_rule":null,"enacted_date":null,"end_date":null,"penalty":"Failure to file the Landlord Declaration makes the eviction a violation of the RSO or JCO. Failure to pay relocation assistance may be raised by the tenant as an affirmative defense in an eviction action.","citation":"LAMC 151.09, 165.03, 165.06 (Los Angeles Municipal Code)","quoted_span":"Relocation Assistance is paid per unit, not per tenant.","supporting_spans":["Payment shall be made available within fifteen (15) days of service of the written notice of eviction; however,","Effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027"],"confidence":0.85,"conflict_note":null},{"jurisdiction":"Los Angeles, CA","level":"city","category":"just_cause_eviction","status":"in_force","title":"LA Resident Protections Ordinance (RPO) relocation for demolition of Protected Units for new construction","requirement":"When a Protected Unit is demolished for new construction, the landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict (JCO units) or a Notice of Intent to Withdraw Units From Rental Housing Use (RSO units) with LAHD. The landlord must serve a written notice and file a copy with LAHD within 3 business days. Relocation must be paid at the higher of State Housing Crisis Act or City amounts, and the RSO/JCO amounts are due within 15 days of the termination notice. Under the RPO the owner chooses one of three relocation options (standardized payment, comparable replacement unit plus RSO/JCO relocation, or individualized relocation). Occupant protections include the right to relocation, the right to remain up to 6 months before construction starts (with a 6-month notice), the right to return if demolition does not proceed, the right of first refusal for some tenants, and tenant notification requirements.","key_value":"Option 1 standardized payments (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027): Extremely Low Income $115,480; Very Low Income $96,750; Low Income $87,450; households above low income are paid under Chart A (RSO/JCO amounts). RPO penalties start at $250,000 per displaced unit.","coverage_conditions":"Applies only to Protected Units to be demolished for new construction, where demolition occurs within 5 years after filing the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict. All RSO units are Protected Units. Protected Units include units subject to affordability covenants or rent control within the past five years, units rented by lower or very low income households within the past five years, and units withdrawn under the Ellis Act within the past 10 years.","exemptions":"If the units to be demolished are not Protected Units or are not occupied by a lower income tenant, the regular RSO or JCO relocation rules apply.","coverage_logic":{"covers":null,"exempt":null},"subject":"landlord","interaction":"Owner must pay the highest applicable relocation amount under State and City law; the RPO codifies and expands the State Housing Crisis Act protections.","yields_to_local":false,"preempts_local":false,"effective_date":"2025-02-11","effective_rule":null,"enacted_date":"2025-02-11","end_date":null,"penalty":"Financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.","citation":"Los Angeles Ordinance Nos. 188481 and 188482 (Resident Protections Ordinance)","quoted_span":"Owners have 3 relocation options to comply with the RPO relocation rules.","supporting_spans":["Tenants Displaced by New Development $115,480 $96,750 $87,450"],"confidence":0.8,"conflict_note":null},{"jurisdiction":"CA","level":"state","category":"just_cause_eviction","status":"in_force","title":"California Housing Crisis Act relocation benefits for lower-income tenants displaced by demolition","requirement":"Under the Housing Crisis Act (HCA), lower income households (80% AMI or lower) displaced by demolition of their units where the owner will replace the units with new construction must receive relocation benefits consistent with those required of public entities under Gov. Code Title 1, Div. 7, Ch. 16 (Section 7260 et seq.). The RSO and JCO relocation amounts must also be enhanced for lower income tenants under the HCA. It covers only the just_cause_eviction category (relocation assistance for no-fault evictions); no in-scope rules appear for the other five categories. Two minor inconsistencies in the document are not material to any rule: the B bulletin's fee chart is labeled July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026 while its relocation charts say July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027, and the bulletin text says copies of notices are filed within '3 days' (A) versus '3 business days' (B). The Ellis Act (Cal. Gov. Code § 7060.4) is mentioned only in passing and is not recorded as a separate rule."}
